narrative: Material PL1__MD9F9B81 exhibits a lumpy, zero-inflated demand pattern (CV=2.10, 39% non-zero days) with a weak downward trend and moderate lead time variability (CV=0.44). The current SAP policy carries zero safety stock and orders at MOQ frequency, incurring excessive ordering costs. The optimized (r,Q) continuous-review policy sets safety stock at 1,999 units to achieve 95% service level and raises the order quantity to the EOQ of 26,171 units, reducing total annual cost by 78.6% while remaining feasible within storage constraints.
warnings: High demand variability detected (CV=2.10) - consider demand segmentation
Demand pattern is lumpy - standard EOQ assumptions may not fully capture stockout risk during burst periods
Storage utilization post-replenishment is 98.2% - limited buffer margin; monitor inbound timing

research_insights.selection_rationale: Lumpy zero-inflated demand with moderate lead time variability is best managed by a continuous-review reorder-point policy that triggers immediately when stock falls to the ROP, preventing prolonged stockouts during sporadic burst demand. Periodic review would risk missing demand spikes within the review window.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage utilization reaches 98.2% immediately after each replenishment (28,170 of 28,697 units). If a delivery arrives earlier than expected while cycle stock is still high, overflow risk exists. Recommend monitoring delivery scheduling closely.
